messages:
opsbot: INCIDENT ALERT — model-family 'aurora' sustained TPM spike exceeding 3x baseline in prod region-us-east-1. Auto-sculpt triggered on aurora-v3, but error rate creeping up for aurora-v2. Immediate triage required. Pager: Marta R.
Marta R.: I'm on it. Seeing large fanout from a handful of API keys — tracing to a 3rd-party integration. ETA 3m for initial mitigation plan.
Elaine: thanks. Can we temporarily tighten per-model TPM for aurora-v3 and aurora-v2 and shape tokens for chat endpoints? Suggest: aurora-v3 tpm -> 2,500 (from 7,500), rpm -> 60; aurora-v2 tpm -> 1,000 (from 3,000).
Samir: agree with shaping. Also want to enable prefix cache bypass to reduce repeated context reprocessing for these keys. I'll prepare commands.
Marta R.: Kevin, can you confirm if customer-facing features (attachments, streaming) tied to these models can be disabled briefly without breaking SDKs? We need to track customer impact.
Kevin: attachments streaming for aurora-family flagged as optional — we can toggle. Support notified for targeted customers with high qps.
Support-Bot: Notifying CS with templated message: "We're applying temporary rate shaping on aurora-family to maintain platform stability. Some users may see reduced throughput for large streaming responses."
Elaine: executing mitigation now. Steps:
```
# set temporary rate limits via controlplane
curl -X POST \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/ratelimits \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"scope":"model","model":"aurora-v3","tpm":2500,"rpm":60,"reason":"prod surge 2176543210"}'
```
Elaine: also setting aurora-v2:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/ratelimits -d '{"model":"aurora-v2","tpm":1000,"rpm":30,"reason":"prod surge 2176543210"}'
```
Samir: I'm pushing a traffic-shaping override to route non-critical low-priority requests to atlas-small fallback. Command: `/runbook route-override --from aurora --to atlas-small --percent 30 --duration 15m --dry-run false`
Marta R.: executing override.
opsbot: Deploy job started: rate-limit-update-service (job id rl-7851). Logs available at https://infra.logs/rl-7851
Elaine: RL update returned 200 for both models. Control plane shows new limits in UI, but runtime nodes show mixed state — some pools still reporting old tokens (KV cache refresh lag).
Samir: forcing runtime KV refresh on affected pools (us-east-1-slice-a,b).
Samir: command run:
```
kubectl exec -n runtime pool-a -- /bin/sh -c "curl -sS http://localhost:8080/internal/refresh-cache?models=aurora-v2,aurora-v3"
```
Marta R.: monitoring error rate and 5xx for aurora-family. Baseline 5xx was 0.3%, currently 1.4% before action.
(2m later)
Marta R.: post-mitigation numbers: overall TPS down ~55% for aurora-v3, 5xx down to 0.45%. RPM/Tokens accepted aligns with new tpm. Latency p95 improved from 1.1s -> 700ms.
Kevin: pushing CS note to customers showing high qps. Templated fragment included in thread.
Support-Bot: CS blast queued to customers: [customer-a@example], [customer-b@example] — message sent.
Elaine: observed a small regression for long-stream clients that expected continuous chunking. Workaround: if you need uninterrupted streaming, set header `x-allow-unthrottled: true` — but it's only for whitelisted enterprise keys.
Marta R.: good, make sure we whitelist any critical enterprise keys if needed. Kevin, can you check the whitelist?
Kevin: checked — enterprise keys E-423 and E-512 already whitelisted. No action needed.
Samir: starting gradual ramp plan: keep current limits for 15m, then increase aurora-v3 tpm -> 4,000 for 10m, monitor. If 5xx stays <0.6% and latency p95 <900ms, revert to normal over next 30m.
Marta R.: documented in incident runbook: incident/2176543210 -> mitigation: temporary per-model rate sculpt, fallback routing, KV refresh, feature toggle for streaming.
opsbot: NOTE: handoff scheduled in 20m to next oncall (Elaine is going off in 15m). Marta, please coordinate handoff with Samir.
Elaine: I'll stay to confirm ramp window, but I need a formal handoff at +20.
Samir: I'll own 2nd-15m window and escalation if error rate climbs.
(10m later)
Marta R.: midpoint check-in: aurora-v3 5xx 0.38%, aurora-v2 0.6%, overall platform healthy. We can try the planned bump to 4,000 tpm now.
Samir: bumping aurora-v3 to 4,000 tpm.
Elaine: applied via controlplane API.
opsbot: change applied rl-7852. Runtime reported partial convergence; monitoring ingest shows small spike but within thresholds.
Kevin: Customer impact log updated: customers with top qps saw increased latency for large streaming tasks; no data loss. CS updated ticketing queue.
Marta R.: approaching handoff. Samir will continue watch. Elaine, if you need to rejoin, ping here.
Elaine: confirmed, I'll be reachable. Handing off: last check: aurora-v3 tpm 4,000, aurora-v2 tpm 1,000, route-override 30% to atlas-small, streaming feature toggle off for non-enterprise.
Samir: acknowledged. I'll escalate to eng-runtime if any pool falls behind in KV convergence; otherwise will let Marta close incident after ramp-to-normal.
Marta R.: closing plan: maintain current until next 15m check, then raise aurora-v3 to 6,000 if steady, then to baseline if safe. Postmortem owner: Marta.
Support-Bot: Tickets auto-created: INC-4332 (customer impact summary), RUN-2176543210 (mitigation runbook entry).
opsbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitoring) — keep thread open for 1 hour for follow-ups.
